sources.title: Publication 969 (2025), Health Savings Accounts and Other Tax-Favored Health Plans
sources.section: Additional contribution at 55 (1,000; § 223(b)(3), not indexed); Additional tax (20% of distributions not used for qualified medical expenses)

sources.title: Schedule 1-A (Form 1040) 2025
sources.section: Part V lines 31 to 37: 6,000 per person aged 65, reduced by 6% of modified AGI over 75,000 (150,000 joint)

sources.title: IRS Fact Sheet FS-2025-03, Working Families Tax Cuts: tax deductions for working Americans and seniors
sources.section: Deduction for Seniors: effective for 2025 through 2028, 6,000 per eligible individual, phased out over 75,000 (150,000 joint)
sources.note: Web page (P.L. 119-21). The old URL .../one-big-beautiful-bill-act-tax-deductions-for-working-americans-and-seniors now redirects here.

sources.title: Publication 915 (2025), Social Security and Equivalent Railroad Retirement Benefits
sources.section: Base amount (25,000 single, 32,000 joint); up to 85% taxable above 34,000 (44,000 joint); Worksheet 1. Statutory (§ 86), not indexed

sources.title: Instructions for Form 8960 (2025)
sources.section: Application to Individuals: 3.8%; thresholds 250,000 joint and 200,000 single (§ 1411, not indexed)

sources.title: Instructions for Form 5329 (2025)
sources.section: Part I: the 10% additional tax on early distributions (§ 72(t))

sources.title: Instructions for Schedule D (Form 1040) 2025
sources.section: Capital Losses: deductible up to gains plus 3,000 (§ 1211(b), not indexed)

sources.title: Publication 15 (2026), (Circular E), Employer's Tax Guide
sources.section: What's New and section 9: social security tax 6.2% to the 2026 wage base limit of 184,500; Medicare tax 1.45%
sources.note: A primary IRS confirmation of the 2026 wage base; the IRS COLA table page (below) lists the same 184,500.

sources.title: IRS COLA increases for dollar limitations on benefits and contributions
sources.section: 2026 column: elective deferrals 24,500, catch-up 8,000 (11,250 at 60 to 63), defined contribution limit 72,000, IRA 7,500 and 1,100, taxable wage base 184,500
sources.note: Web page, last reviewed 2026-08-24; 2026 is still its newest year on the retrieval date.

sources.title: IRS Topic no. 560, Additional Medicare Tax
sources.section: 0.9% on Medicare wages over 250,000 (married filing jointly) or 200,000 (single); not indexed

sources.title: SSA, Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) information (2026 amounts)
sources.section: COLA 2.8% first paid January 2026; retirement earnings test 24,480 a year under full retirement age, 65,160 in the year it is reached
sources.note: www.ssa.gov refuses automated requests. Secondary (two independent published sources agree, by web search on 2026-11-13): the COLA in CRS report 94-803 (edition of 2026-05-27, congress.gov) and in the SSA computation quoted by web search (Q3 2025 CPI-W 317.265 against 308.729); the earnings-test amounts in Kiplinger's expert guide to the earnings test (2,040 and 5,430 a month in 2026, that is 24,480 and 65,160 a year) and in the 2027 SSA fact sheet as quoted by web search ('up from $24,480'; BenefitsUSA's summary: 'up from $65,160 in 2026'). The 2026 wage base is primary (Publication 15 above).
